title: py-stellar-base decodes a bool encoded as 2 as true, as stellar-core does (the network's reading, not a defect)

target.versions_affected: none: the SDK reads the value as stellar-core does

caps_note: No CAP applies: an XDR encoding rule that holds in every protocol version (the corpus's xdr-strict group).

entries.expected: reject: an XDR bool is 0 or 1 (RFC 4506 4.4)
entries.observed: Executed on 17.0.0 and 17.0.1 (xdrlib3 0.1.1): xdr.SCVal.from_xdr_bytes decodes the value as True and re-encodes it as 0000000000000001, the same reading as stellar-core 30.0.0.

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner (xcc conform run --columns 'python@*' --entries 'xdr-strict/bool-value-2'), L0: accepts_invalid, declared as a wont_fix known divergence.
evidence.expected_basis: RFC 4506 4.4; stellar-core 30.0.0 print-xdr reads the same bytes as TRUE (evidence/core-print-xdr/out/bool-2.txt).

history.note: Created from the Python cells of xdr-strict/bool-value-2.
The SDK reads the bytes as the network does; recorded as wont_fix on the entry.

resolution.reason: Not a defect in py-stellar-base. The SDK accepts a bool encoded as 2 and reads it as True, which RFC 4506 does not allow, but stellar-core 30.0.0 reads the same bytes the same way (print-xdr shows "b": "TRUE", evidence/core-print-xdr/out/bool-2.txt; xdrpp reads any non-zero bool as true) and re-serialises it canonically. A reader that agrees with the network's own decoder shows the value the network applies, so there is nothing to change; the entry keeps its strict expectation and the cell is declared.
resolution.manifest_action: divergence recorded as wont_fix on xdr-strict/bool-value-2 (stellar-sdk (PyPI) 17.0.0 || 17.0.1), naming this record
